comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I’m John, the solo maker behind Talanoa. Funny enough, Talanoa was never supposed to become a product. I originally built it just for myself. I spend a huge part of my day in email, but I never really liked using traditional email clients. So instead of looking for yet another one, I started building the inbox I wanted for myself. Then I showed it to a few friends. They loved it. They started using it. And eventually, they put enough pressure on me to turn my little personal project into a real product. So… here we are. Along the way, one idea became increasingly obvious to me: Email is a conversation that forgot it was one. A thread between two people is basically a chat. A message, a reply, a reply to the reply. Yet email clients still show repeated quotes, signatures, headers, footers and years of clutter. So I rebuilt Talanoa around a different idea: what if email felt more like a messenger? Today, Talanoa turns your inbox into clean, chat-like conversations, while keeping everything that makes email, email. But it goes further: 💬 Emails become actual conversations ✅ Any email can become a todo with a next step and due date 📅 Your calendar lives alongside your conversations ✨ AI helps you search, summarize and write, entirely on-device 📥 Gmail, Outlook, iCloud and IMAP accounts can live in one inbox 🔒 No cloud sync, no tracking. Your emails stay on your computer. I’ve been building Talanoa independently, talking to users, breaking things, rebuilding them, and questioning quite a few assumptions we’ve had about email for the last 30 years. What started as a tool I built for myself has slowly become something much bigger, and this version finally feels like the Talanoa I always wanted to use. I’d genuinely love your feedback, especially on one thing: Does the “email as a conversation” approach change the way you feel about your inbox? And if there’s one thing your current email client does that you couldn’t live without, tell me. I’m listening 👇 Thanks for checking out Talanoa ❤️ John

today.description: Navige uses Sufficiency Intelligence to cut AI agent costs while work runs. It sends suitable requests to smaller models, caches repeated reads and trims bulky tool results. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋Why we built NavigeMost of what an AI agent does isn’t hard - sorting an email, pulling a date out of a document, picking the next step. But often, it all runs on the most expensive model, because that’s the one written into the code and nobody went back to change it.Then the bill arrives as one number, and nobody can say which agent spent what.Navige sits in front of calls routed through it and acts before they run, while the cost can still change. We call this Sufficiency Intelligence: give each task exactly the intelligence it needs.How it worksIt assesses each request and sends suitable ones to a smaller model. Your model is the ceiling: Navige only moves calls down, never up, and keeps yours whenever it’s unsure.If the smaller model fumbles a tool call, the call re-runs on your original model, and your agent only sees that answer.It records every job: what it cost, what the controls changed and what made the difference. Measured savings and estimates are clearly separated.On top of that, you get budgets per team and per job, approval holds for risky actions, a kill switch and an audit trail.Two things we did on purposeWatchtower is the starting point. Navige watches and shows what it would have done, but changes nothing until you say so.Connect your Anthropic or AWS Bedrock account and put your real bill next to Navige’s figures, so you can check the numbers instead of trusting a savings claim.PricingWatchtower is free forever. On paid plans, of the measured savings Navige can show, you keep four parts and we keep one, subject to a $9/month minimum.Give it a weekWatch your agents for a week. Nothing changes until you decide.Which of your agents’ jobs do you suspect is running on a much bigger model than it needs? 👇

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I’m Chris, co-founder of withHuman along with Ece 👋 Before withHuman, we built an AI agent that investigated production issues and worked out fixes. It could often find the right fix. The hard part was asking a customer to let it apply that fix to their production systems. Fair enough: nobody wants to hand an agent admin access to production and hope for the best. We added an approval step, but the same problems kept coming up in conversations. Each team had different rules about who could approve what. They wanted finer control over what the agent could do. And they were already using other agents, each with its own approval setup. withHuman is what we wished existed back then. It sits between your agents and their tools and intercepts each tool call before it runs. Your rules approve or deny the routine ones automatically, and the risky ones go to the right person, wherever suits them. Your agents don’t need to change, and they can’t skip it. What’s available today: • The Agent Approval Protocol (AAP), an open spec, with prebuilt hooks for Claude Code and Codex, and SDKs for Python and TypeScript • withHuman itself, open source, with a hosted version that has a free plan The quickest way to try it is the Quickstart, which connects a coding agent you already use in a few minutes. There’s plenty we’re still figuring out, like giving reviewers enough context to decide, and gating calls that don’t go through MCP. We wrote more about that here: https://withhuman.ai/blog/introd... We’d love your feedback, especially on this: which of your agent’s actions would you want a human to sign off on first? Ece and Chris

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Nikita, and this is Tiden, the product we've been building for the past year. It's for engineering teams shipping agent-written code every day who want to let agents do the coding while keeping control of what ships.Qase is a software testing platform used by tens of thousands of builders, and 9 years of building it for them taught us a lot about how quality work gets done. Last year that changed on our own team: agents started producing most of the code, and the rest of our process didn't speed up with it. Review, testing, release, keeping requirements current: all of it became bottlenecks.Other engineering teams tell the same story. A gaming publisher I talked to, with about 1k+ developers, saw pull request volume go up 4 to 5 times while the number of features they shipped stayed flat. A payments company described 10 times the coding output and 10% more delivery.The problem underneath itAn agent session produces the code, the tests that pass on that code, and the docs describing what it built. The next session reads those docs as fact. Every artifact agrees with every other one, because they all came from the same place. A QA automation lead at a tax and accounting platform put it best: "If you have an agent that decides what to build, and then another agent is grading what's being built against what was actually built, you're essentially encoding the wrong thing. Your tests will pass, they'll be green, but it wasn’t what you wanted."The two usual fixes, another rules file in the repo and better AI code review, both sit inside that same loop. The judge has to sit outside it.What Tiden doesTiden is that judge. It's intent verification for coding agents: it sits beside your agents, whichever ones you use, and verifies that what they built is what you actually asked for. It keeps that intent as specs, versioned like code, and checks every change against them rather than against the session that produced it.Every agent session becomes a closed loop:A session hook captures what you asked for before the first editThe change comes back as a requirement for you to review; requirements branch and merge like codeTiden picks the tests the change touches, runs them in your environment, and the agent fixes what fails before anything mergesThe gate is tied to the spec. Red tells the agent what to fix. Green is a pass you can defend, with the evidence attachedIn production, an error traces back to the release, the change and the prompt behind it, and the fix comes with the test that was missingTiden works beside Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Copilot, and belongs to none of them. Specs live as one versioned record every agent reads from, instead of a growing pile of markdown. You set the thresholds and the gates, and a person approves anything the loop can't settle.One limit, stated plainly: Tiden checks the work against what you asked for. Whether you asked for the right thing is still a human judgment.Get startedTiden is live at https://tiden.ai. The CLI installs in one command, the docs are at https://docs.tiden.ai, and Starter and Team both come with a 14-day free trial. If you'd rather talk to us first, there's a short form on the site: https://tiden.ai/contact.What I'd like from youHonest feedback over upvotes. Where does your team feel this gap most: review, regression, release, or production? What would make you trust an external check?

week.name: Google EmbeddingGemma 2
week.tagline: An open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
week.description: EmbeddingGemma 2 is Google DeepMind's open embedding model that maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared space, so you can search across them from a single query. At 740M parameters it runs on-device, needing about 567MB of RAM on a Pixel 11 Pro for the full multimodal model (191MB for text only). Apache 2.0 licensed, with weights on Hugging Face and Kaggle. comments.text: EmbeddingGemma 2 is Google DeepMind's open, lightweight multimodal embedding model. It maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared space and is small enough to run on a phone.Problem: Searching by meaning usually needs a pipeline of separate models: a captioning model for images, speech-to-text for audio, a text embedder on top. That's slow, memory-hungry, and often sends your data to the cloud. For private, on-device apps, that's a hard trade-off.Solution: One 740M-parameter model, built on the Gemma 4 architecture, that embeds all five types of content in the same space. A text query can find a photo, and a voice memo can find a video clip. Everything runs locally, so your data never has to leave the device.What makes it different: It's modular. You can load only the encoders you need, as little as 270M parameters for text and code, plus optional vision (170M) and audio (300M) encoders. With quantization on a Pixel 11 Pro, it needs about 191MB of RAM for text only and about 567MB for the full multimodal model. It shares its tokenizer and audio encoder with Gemma 4, so running both together uses less memory than running them separately.Key features:Text, code, images, video and audio in a single embedding space8K token context (4x EmbeddingGemma 1), enough for about 5.5 minutes of audio, 29 images or 58 video framesVectors can be shrunk from 768 to 512, 256 or 128 dimensions for up to 6x less storageCode retrieval improves from 68.76 to 78.68 on MTEB Code (+9.92 points)Google says it leads sub-1B multimodal embedding models on benchmarks like MTEB Code and MAEB (audio)Can also act as a zero-shot, on-device decision engine: Google's MediaPipe demo scores 500 options per turn in a chess game in under 100 msWorks with transformers, sentence-transformers, MLX, vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang, Ollama, LMStudio, Qdrant and UnslothWho it's for: Developers building private, offline-capable search, RAG, media retrieval or local codebase search, and anyone who wants cross-modal search without a cloud dependency. week.aiReview:
### مسئله و راه‌حل
فرآیند فروش محصولات فنی و B۲B معمولاً زمان‌بر و پراکنده است. کارشناسان فروش مجبورند بین ابزارهای تحقیق، CRM، فایل‌های متنی و اسلایدهای ارائه جابجا شوند که این امر باعث از دست رفتن بافت اطلاعاتی (Context) می‌شود. kōdlo با ارائه یک فضای کاری یکپارچه متصل به حافظه مشترک هوش مصنوعی، تمام مراحل از لیدیابی، تحقیق، تولید محتوای شخصی‌سازی‌شده تا ساخت ارائه‌ها را در یک محیط انجام می‌دهد.

### معماری و تکنولوژی
نقطه عطف فنی این ابزار، استفاده از استاندارد Model Context Protocol (MCP) است که به کاربر اجازه می‌دهد بافت اطلاعاتی موجود در kōdlo را به Claude Desktop یا سایر ایجنت‌های هوش مصنوعی متصل کند. معماری سیستم بر پایه RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) متکی است تا اسناد بارگذاری شده را آنالیز کرده و با ارجاع دقیق به شماره صفحه، پاسخ دهد.

### مدل درآمدی
این محصول از مدل اشتراکی SaaS (پلن‌های Starter و پیشرفته) استفاده می‌کند و با پیشنهاد تخفیف در پروداکت هانت، جذب مشتریان اولیه را هدف قرار داده است.

### نقاط قوت
۱. حافظه یکپارچه میان ایجنت‌ها و کاربر
۲. پشتیبانی از پروتکل MCP جهت اتصال به سایر ایجنت‌ها
۳. خروجی‌های واقعی و قابل استفاده مانند فایل‌های PPTX و PDF اختصاصی
۴. ارجاع دقیق به منابع در بخش Knowledge Hub

### نقاط ضعف
۱. وابستگی شدید به کیفیت دیتابیس‌های B۲B برای یافتن سیگنال‌های فروش
۲. احتمال وجود پیام‌های اسپم در صورت عدم نظارت انسانی بر پیام‌های خروجی

### نکته طلایی برای ایران
در بازار ایران، مشکل اصلی عدم وجود یک دیتابیس جامع مثل Crunchbase برای B۲B است. نسخه ایرانی می‌تواند تمرکز خود را روی **مرکز دانش اسناد سازمانی (RAG اختصاصی محصولات)** و **تولید خودکار پیش‌نویس استعلام قیمت و پروپوزال‌های مناقصات** بگذارد که چالش اصلی شرکت‌های B۲B داخلی است.

Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
